# **1\. Executive Summary**

Kecktech IT Solutions LLC is a disability-owned, family-operated managed IT services provider headquartered in Park City, Kansas. The company operates a purpose-built, 100% solar-powered private data center and delivers five integrated technology services to small and medium-sized businesses and senior citizens in the greater Wichita metropolitan area.

Kecktech's core competitive advantage is the integration of renewable energy infrastructure, data sovereignty, AI-assisted custom application development, refurbished hardware deployment, and human-centered accessibility design into a single, locally owned platform. No regional competitor offers this combination.

## **1.1  The Opportunity**

Two underserved markets define Kecktech's initial client base. First, small and medium-sized businesses in the Wichita MSA that are overpaying for fragmented cloud software subscriptions and lack affordable access to private data hosting or custom application development. Second, senior citizens who face escalating technology-based fraud, inaccessible interfaces, and no local, trustworthy IT support option. Kecktech is uniquely positioned to serve both segments simultaneously through its five-service model.

# **3\. The Problem We Solve**

Kecktech was designed around four market failures that the mainstream IT industry has shown no interest in resolving. Each represents a significant, underserved opportunity.

## **3.1  The SaaS Subscription Burden on Small Business**

The average U.S. small business pays $800–$1,200 per month for a fragmented portfolio of cloud software subscriptions. Customer relationship management, accounting, scheduling, team communication, project management, and HR tools are each procured from separate vendors, licensed separately, and often used well below 30% of their available capacity. Total estimated annual SaaS waste across U.S. small businesses exceeds $30 billion.

Artificial intelligence has fundamentally changed the economics of custom software development. Tools that previously required a six-month development engagement at $50,000 or more can now be built in two to four weeks by an experienced AI-assisted developer, at a fraction of the cost. Small businesses have not yet systematically accessed this advantage — Kecktech positions itself as the bridge.

## **3.2  Data Sovereignty and Private Hosting Demand**

Following a succession of high-profile data breaches affecting millions of small businesses, 67% of SMB owners report a preference for private data hosting but cite cost and technical complexity as prohibitive barriers. Hyperscale cloud providers — Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud — operate under broad terms of service that grant them the right to scan, analyze, and in some cases share customer data. For medical, legal, and financial service businesses, this creates active compliance exposure.

Kecktech offers Kansas-based, solar-powered, privately-hosted data infrastructure at a price point accessible to small businesses. Client data does not leave the facility. The hosting platform is HIPAA-ready by design.

## **3.3  Senior Citizens and Technology Vulnerability**

54 million Americans aged 65 and older represent one of the fastest-growing technology user segments and one of the most systematically underserved. The FBI's 2023 Internet Crime Report documented $3.4 billion in senior-targeted technology fraud — an 11% increase over the prior year. AI-generated voice cloning, phishing, and remote access scams have become sophisticated enough to defeat defenses that adequately protect younger users.

Mass-market MSPs have no economic model for serving senior clients. The margin is thin, the relationship is intensive, and the communication style required is fundamentally different from corporate IT support. Kecktech's disability-informed, accessibility-first service culture is a genuine competitive advantage in this segment.

## **3.4  Electronic Waste and Grid-Dependent IT Infrastructure**

The global IT industry generates approximately 50 million metric tons of electronic waste annually. Enterprise organizations systematically replace servers, workstations, and networking equipment at 3–5 year intervals despite 80–90% remaining functional capacity. This hardware enters a waste stream that, even when formally recycled, generates significant environmental and economic cost.

Simultaneously, the data centers that power modern cloud computing operate predominantly on carbon-intensive grid electricity. Kecktech's 100% solar-powered infrastructure and circular economy hardware model directly address both dimensions of this problem — creating measurable ESG impact alongside commercial returns.

# **4\. Products & Services**

Kecktech delivers five integrated services from a single solar-powered facility. The integration is the product — clients can access IT support, hardware, custom software, secure hosting, and senior care from one locally-owned, relationship-based provider.

## **4.1  White Glove Managed IT Services (MSP)**

Kecktech's flagship service provides small businesses with comprehensive, SLA-backed remote IT support delivered by the co-founders themselves and directly supervised staff. Every client is assigned a dedicated point of contact. There are no offshore call centers, no automated ticket queues without human review, and no sub-contracting of critical support functions.

### **Service Level Agreement**

| Priority | Response SLA | Definition | Examples |
| ----- | :---: | ----- | ----- |
| **P1 — Critical** | **2 hours** | Total service outage, data loss risk, active security breach | Server down, ransomware detected, complete connectivity failure |
| **P2 — High** | **4 hours** | Major function impaired, multiple users affected | Email system down, critical application error, VPN failure |
| **P3 — Standard** | **24 hours** | Single user issue, non-critical system fault | Workstation configuration, software update, peripheral setup |

### **Pricing Structure**

* Standard MSP Plan: $199/month per client — includes unlimited remote support tickets, monthly security audit, patch management, and backup monitoring

* Managed Security Add-On: $49/month — enhanced endpoint protection, email filtering, dark web monitoring

* On-Site Support (if required): $95/hour — Sedgwick County only, scheduled 72 hours in advance

## **4.2  Hardware-as-a-Service (HaaS)**

Kecktech provides enterprise-grade refurbished computing hardware to small businesses on a monthly subscription basis. Every unit is sourced from certified refurbishment channels, tested to Tier-1 performance specifications, zero-wiped per NIST 800-88 standards, and configured before delivery.

The HaaS model eliminates the capital expenditure of hardware procurement for small businesses while ensuring they operate on current, supported equipment. End-of-life units re-enter Kecktech's refurbishment pipeline — creating a true circular economy for business hardware.

### **HaaS Fleet Specifications**

* Launch fleet: 20 units — Dell OptiPlex and HP EliteDesk refurbished enterprise workstations

* Year 2 expansion: 60 units; Year 3 target: 150 units

* Each unit includes: certified OS installation, security hardening, remote management agent, 90-day hardware warranty

* Monthly fee: $149/unit — includes hardware, monitoring, next-business-day swap for failed units

* E-waste compliance: full chain-of-custody documentation from intake through deployment or certified recycling

## **4.3  AI Custom Application Development**

Kecktech's AI Custom Application Development service builds lightweight, purpose-built business applications that permanently replace expensive SaaS subscription stacks. Advances in AI-assisted development tools have reduced the time required to build production-quality business applications by 70–80%, making custom software economically accessible to small businesses for the first time.

Clients own their code. Kecktech does not impose licensing fees, subscription requirements, or vendor lock-in. The application is delivered as the client's intellectual property, hosted on Kecktech's sovereign servers if desired.

### **Applications Built and Deployed**

* Custom CRM systems — replacing Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho ($150–$300/month saved per client)

* Accounting and invoicing tools — replacing QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Wave ($80–$180/month saved)

* Appointment scheduling platforms — replacing Calendly, Acuity, Square Appointments ($30–$80/month saved)

* Internal communication suites — replacing Slack, Microsoft Teams for small team use cases ($50–$180/month saved)

* Workflow automation tools — replacing Zapier, Make, Monday.com ($50–$200/month saved)

* Healthcare and legal compliance portals — HIPAA-ready, Kansas-hosted, built for small practice requirements

### **Pricing, Timeline, and Client Economics**

| ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Starter Business Suite | $3,000 | 2 weeks | $300–$500 | Less than 10 months |

**Cross-Sell Economics:**  A client who receives a $5,000 custom build and adds Sovereign Hosting ($49/month) plus White Glove MSP ($199/month) generates $2,976/year in recurring revenue in addition to the one-time build fee. Customer lifetime value for this profile over 48 months: $19,304.

## **4.4  Senior Technology Concierge**

The Senior Technology Concierge is a subscription-based, white-glove IT service designed specifically for adults aged 65 and older. The service is built around accessibility, patience, plain-language communication, and proactive fraud protection — not reactive ticket resolution.

### **Service Inclusions at $79/Month**

* Monthly device health check — proactive review of device performance, software currency, and security status

* Scam and phishing interception — managed email and phone filtering, real-time scam call blocking

* Video call setup and support — family communication platforms configured and maintained

* Emergency IT response — same-business-day response for fraud incidents, device compromise, or access lockout

* Quarterly in-depth security review — report shared with family members if authorized by the senior client

* Plain-language documentation — all instructions written for non-technical audiences, large-print available

## **4.5  Sovereign Private Hosting**

Kecktech offers Kansas-based, solar-powered private server hosting for businesses that require data residency within the state, HIPAA compliance, or an alternative to hyperscale cloud vendors. Client data is hosted exclusively within the Kecktech facility in Park City, Kansas. It does not traverse third-party cloud infrastructure.

* Standard hosting: $49/month — up to 500GB storage, SSL, automated backups, 99.5% uptime SLA

* Business hosting: $149/month — up to 5TB, dedicated resources, HIPAA-ready configuration, 99.9% SLA

* Custom enterprise tier: priced on specification — for multi-TB, compliance-heavy, or high-availability requirements

## **8.2  Energy Operations and Solar Strategy**

* The 25kW solar array is designed to meet 95%+ of facility power demand under standard Kansas solar irradiance conditions (300+ annual peak sun hours)

* The 100kWh LiFePO4 battery bank provides approximately 8 hours of zero-grid facility operation at full server load

* The Battery Management System (BMS) manages charge cycles, load balancing, generator handoff, and provides real-time monitoring accessible to the founders remotely

* Compute-intensive workloads — VM snapshots, batch processing, large AI development builds — are scheduled during 08:00–16:00 peak solar generation hours to minimize battery draw

* Monthly energy audit: the Kecktech team produces a kWh-per-client efficiency report used for ESG investor reporting and continuous improvement

## **8.3  Circular Economy and E-Waste Standards**

* 100% of client hardware is sourced from certified enterprise refurbishment channels — zero new hardware procurement

* All units are zero-wiped per NIST SP 800-88 media sanitization standards prior to redeployment

* End-of-life hardware re-enters the Kecktech refurbishment pipeline; units not suitable for redeployment are transferred to certified e-waste processors with documented chain of custody

* Annual Circular Economy Report published for investors, grant bodies, and ESG stakeholders — documenting units processed, diversion rates, and carbon offset equivalents

* Year 1 target: 80% diversion of all hardware processed from landfill stream

# **11\. Grant & Non-Dilutive Incentive Strategy**

Kecktech occupies a rare intersection of federal and state grant eligibility categories simultaneously. The company is disability-owned, rural-located, renewable-energy-powered, circular-economy-operating, and IT-workforce-developing. This multi-layered eligibility creates a non-dilutive capital opportunity that materially de-risks the investor position.

| Program | Type | Value | Target Date | Eligibility Basis |
| ----- | ----- | :---: | :---: | ----- |
| **USDA REAP** | Federal Grant | **Up to $1M** | Q2 2026 | Rural Energy for America Program — covers 25% of solar array and battery cost. Park City, KS qualifies as rural. Application begins with Letter of Intent. |
| **IRA § 48E ITC** | Fed Tax Credit | **30–40%** | With 2025 return | Investment Tax Credit on solar system placed in service. Energy Community adder (+10%) may apply to Park City ZIP code. Filed via IRS Form 3468\. |
| **WOTC** | Fed Tax Credit | **$2,400–$9,600** | Per hire, ongoing | Work Opportunity Tax Credit — both co-founders qualify under disability category. Filed via IRS Form 8850 at time of hire. |
| **Section 44 ADA Credit** | Fed Tax Credit | **Up to $5,000/yr** | Annual (Form 8826\) | 50% credit on $250–$10,250 in qualifying ADA accessibility improvements to facility, workstations, and assistive technology. |
| **SBA 504 Green Loan** | SBA Loan | **Up to $5M** | Ongoing | Below-market fixed-rate financing (\~6.0%) for green energy infrastructure. Pairs directly with USDA REAP to cover remaining capital gap after grants are applied. |
| **Kansas PACE Program** | State Financing | Project-based | Ongoing | Property Assessed Clean Energy — commercial solar financed through property tax assessment with no upfront capital required. |

# **12\. Risk Analysis & Mitigation**

| Risk Factor | Level | Likelihood / Context | Mitigation Strategy |
| ----- | :---: | ----- | ----- |
| Construction delays or cost overruns | **High** | Moderate — Kansas weather and permitting variability | 12-week buffer built into timeline; fixed-bid contractor agreements; 8% contingency line in capital budget; Sedgwick County pre-application filed |
| Year 1 client ramp slower than projected | **Medium** | Moderate — 20 LOI commitments partially mitigate | 20 founding clients signed LOIs pre-launch; referral incentive program; founding-member pricing locks in early adopters; bridge capital covers 6-month ramp gap |
| AI development capacity at 4 builds per month | **Medium** | Low — AI tools accelerate delivery to 2–4 weeks | Year 2 budget includes contract developer support; builds are scoped and fixed-fee to prevent scope creep; 4-build monthly cap enforced in Year 1 |
| Solar underperformance or equipment failure | **Low** | Low — 25-year panel lifespan, 10-year performance warranty | 100kWh battery provides 8-hour zero-grid buffer; 12kW natural gas generator handles extended outages; SLA uptime backed by commercial property and cyber insurance |
| IRA or REAP policy changes | **Low** | Low — ITC locked by legislation through 2032 | REAP application filed immediately post-funding to lock in current program terms; ITC filed with first-year tax return; Kansas PACE is state-level backstop |
| Key person risk — 2-person team | **Medium** | Moderate — both founders are essential | Cross-training on all systems from Day 1; documented runbook for all critical operations; Year 2 plan includes hiring one junior support technician |
